USB has a couple of different modes that you could look into. I.E. USB Host mode and USB guest mode.

They are important for what they can do. Some USB ports/devices can act as a "host" others as a "guest".

Ex. A standard usb stick for storing data will operate in usb guest mode. You can not use it to "mount" another usb device.

A typical computer can work in usb Host mode. This means that it can "mount" or act on/modify a usb guest device.

In the solution you are considering you are going to need one port to act as a host (connected to a keyboard) and another as a guest (a fake, emulated keyboard). Then you will need some software sitting between to monitor the keystrokes to trigger pre-programmed macros.
